thread:
casey (Support): Customer @AcmeReports reports sudden 401 invalid_api_key immediately after rotating their key in the Console. They say rotation completed but their app returns 401. Can SRE/Eng take a look?

neil (Eng): Can you paste repro steps / what the app expects to find in k8s? Is this hosted vs dedicated?

casey (Support): Repro I used on a staging cluster:
```
# Rotate key via Console -> backend creates logical secret name: redwood-key
# Our cluster is using secrets-store CSI to sync to k8s; it writes a Secret named with namespace suffix
kubectl get secret redwood-key-staging -n staging -o yaml
# Secret data keys: "apikey-staging"
# Deployment env expects:
env:
  - name: REDWOOD_API_KEY
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef:
        name: redwood-key
        key: token
```
Result: app can't find secret/key -> downstream requests 401 invalid_api_key.

kira (SRE): Checking the cluster now — confirmed. Our CSI `secretObjects[].secretName` template currently appends `-{{ .Namespace }}` to avoid collisions, so Console rotation created redwood-key but CSI created `redwood-key-staging`. Deployments that reference the unsuffixed name break after rotation. This isn't a payload corruption, it's a name/key mapping mismatch.

neil (Eng): Ah — the secret key name inside the Secret also changed (`apikey-staging` vs `token`), so two mismatches: secret resource name and key name. How was the app originally reading the secret (whole secret mount vs specific key)?

casey (Support): The customer used `valueFrom.secretKeyRef` pointing to `redwood-key`/`token`. The secrets-store object uses `secretObjects[].data` to map to `apikey-{{ .Namespace }}` by default. So rotation path produced a new resource layout that the deployment isn't expecting.

kira (SRE): Short-term mitigation: create a k8s Secret with the exact name/key the deployment expects and populate it with the rotated key so the app can resume:
```bash
kubectl create secret generic redwood-key \
  --from-literal=token='REDACTED_ROTATED_KEY' -n staging --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```
That will satisfy most env mounts immediately.

neil (Eng): Long-term fixes: (1) make the CSI secretObjects secretName deterministic (no auto-namespace suffix) or (2) standardize the `data[].key` mapping so `token` is used instead of `apikey-<ns>`, or (3) update Helm chart to point env to the computed suffixed name. We'll open a PR for helm chart values: `secretNameSuffix` optional.

casey (Support): I'll relay workaround to the customer and create a support ticket with reproduction steps + suggested remediation commands. They also asked we add guidance to rotation docs.

kira (SRE): I'll file an infra ticket to add a check in our rotation playbook: when rotating keys for clusters using secrets-store CSI with templated names, ensure the k8s Secret name/key matches what deployments expect. Adding a small healthcheck that reads REDWOOD_API_KEY from an example deployment would catch regressions.

deploy-bot: Deploy complete — chart update `make-suffix-configurable` merged and promoted to prod clusters (chart v1.2.5). Monitor for any further 401 reports.

casey (Support): Thanks team — customer acknowledged the workaround and will let us know if any more 401s crop up. :thumbsup:
